doc.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001

chapter: Billy Taylor years and the greats
title: Billy Taylor trio as the best time of his life
summary: May joined Billy Taylor around 1951, enjoyed the brotherly trio, and played Minton's, recorded with Trane and played with Miles and Parker.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: This was about what — you played with Billy Taylor most of the 50s, right?
In the early 50s. I started with him around 1951 I think.
So there was a pretty healthy recording and live music scene at that time.

Oh yeah, oh wonderful. You know when people ask me now to go back in your life and pick out a time that you really, the time that you most enjoyed, and I would have to say the time I spent with Billy. Because not only was it a good trio and playing good music and all like that, it was a real brotherly kind of thing that we had, Billy and I had, and also I was playing — when Billy wasn’t working — I was playing up at Minton’s with all kinds of wonderful people, Carmen McRae and Tony Scott and playing with all these wonderful people. And I recorded with Trane during that time, and played with Miles Davis’ band and I played with Charlie Parker’s band. So it was a wonderful time for me. © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
